title: Trapped in "Limbo"
subtitle: The depths of a soul trapped in the past.

items.speaker: Child
items.text: Mama, when will you be back?

items.speaker: Doctor
items.text: Before you know it, Vanya.

items.speaker: Child
items.text: Will I see you tomorrow? Mama? Mama?
Maxim's Subconsciousness

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Can you hear me, Vertin?

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: As I feared, the dream is unstable. There's abnormal data mixed in with Maxim's fading memories.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I presume it's coming from the polymer.
It's a strange, dilapidated room. Through the doorway, it seems to lead to another seemingly identical room, and then another, and another, as though it were a maze of mirrors.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I hear you, Mesmer. I think the room I'm in must be Maxim's home.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: This dream is likely to be different from anything you've ever handled before. I don't know what lies ahead.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'll be ready. Just keep things running up there.
A stately grandfather clock tolls in the time, and with it, a woman appears by the dining table.

items.speaker: Rozaliya
items.text: Hurry up, Vanya.
Maxim trudges through the doorway and sits down at the table, not as a child, but as a full-grown man.

items.speaker: Rozaliya
items.text: You'll have to head straight to school after breakfast. Remember what I told you?

items.speaker: Rozaliya
items.text: "Wash your hands, keep your mask on, and apply disinfectant as soon as you get home." That's right!
The woman holds up another finger with each reminder. It's the gentle sing-song instruction of a mother to her young child—completely oblivious to his apparent age.
After that, the woman turns to the sink and goes through the motions of washing a dish, yet there is nothing in her hands. A moment later, she answers an unheard question.

items.speaker: Rozaliya
items.text: No. Mama probably won't be home tonight, neither will Papa.

items.speaker: Rozaliya
items.text: Have you finished? Off to school then. Let the teachers know right away if you feel ill, understood?
The woman removes her apron and dons a doctor's coat as she bids Maxim a simple, affectionate goodbye.
As she leaves, Maxim rises from his seat and stretches toward the grandfather clock. He pulls delicately on the minute hand, forcing it back counterclockwise.

items.speaker: Rozaliya
items.text: Hurry up, Vanya.
Maxim re-enters from the same door and sits at the dining table again.
Everything proceeds just as it had before, a repeated moment, frozen in time.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: This subliminal space bears notable similarities to Limbo.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Limbo? Like in the Divine Comedy?

items.speaker: Left
items.text: The name was chosen based on its similarity to the liminal spiritual realm. We use it to refer to subconscious spaces generated by polymerized individuals.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: It appears that this bears a strong resemblance to the space created by your Artificial Somnambulism device.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: However, it is not clear if this space is in fact Limbo, or a dream, or some reflection of them both.
Maxim does not react to their conversation, nor indeed even to his mother.
He simply returns to the clock, time after time, winding the moment back.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: We're on a deadline, remember. We need to induce Maxim to recall his password.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: But try not to push him too hard. There's no telling what additional stress might do to the dream state. We're already operating in the margins.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: Maybe start by collecting clues from the surroundings.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: This moment must be from Maxim's childhood. Do you have any idea what's going on?

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Speculation: This appears to be during the early months of the Plague. During this time, hospitals were overloaded, and doctors were often forced to work long hours isolated in quarantine zones.
As they talk, the clock's hands suddenly speed up, fast-forwarding the scene in the room until it chimes again.
*dong*
Maxim still sits at the dining table, staring out into the void.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Do you hear that?

items.speaker: Left
items.text: They're announcing funerals, Comrade Doctor.
Maxim turns toward the door, his face expressionless and hollow. Cries seem to come from all sides of the room.

items.speaker: Andrey
items.text: Come here, Vanya. Don't be afraid.
A man resembling Maxim crouches in front of him, hugging an invisible figure.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That must be Maxim's father.

items.speaker: Andrey
items.text: Your mama is fine. I got a call from her earlier. She's just too busy to come home.

items.speaker: Andrey
items.text: You know, your mama is very brave. She is doing a great service for us all. Someone must go to the hospitals and take care of all the sick.

items.speaker: Andrey
items.text: I know you miss her, so do I, but there are others that need her more than we do now.
Andrey speaks gently to the invisible figure.

items.speaker: Andrey
items.text: Now, your papa has a job to do too. So, you must stay here and take good care of yourself until we get back.

items.speaker: Andrey
items.text: Don't worry about me, son. I'll send our little robot round to say hi whenever I can.
The man produces a small robot from his pocket. It looks identical to the one in Maxim's family photo.

items.speaker: Andrey
items.text: That sickness has hurt many people, but your papa will do something to stop it.

items.speaker: Andrey
items.text: Since robots never get sick, we'll have them keep the world spinning.

items.speaker: Andrey
items.text: That is how we will save our land and our people.
Andrey passes the invisible figure the little robot, though it disappears as soon as it leaves his hand.

items.speaker: Andrey
items.text: Promise me you'll take good care of yourself, Vanya.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: The number of deaths had already exceeded 20 million at this point. Soviet society was on the verge of collapse.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: And the death toll continued to rise until Dr. Sechenov helped to invent the Redemption vaccine using his polymer.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Heh.
Maxim at last seems to react to their presence, though he does not turn to face them.
Andrey leaves, and the clock's hands speed up once more. Maxim returns to the dining table.
*knock* The door opens. Two men in protective suits enter the room. Before they say anything, that same near-invisible presence rushes over to hug them. Yet they seem to push it away.

items.speaker: Government Employee
items.text: You're mistaken, comrade. We're not your parents.
They seem to have heard something and look at each other.

items.speaker: Government Employee
items.text: Listen, son, can you gather up your family's papers? Then you'll need to come with us.

items.speaker: Government Employee
items.text: Your parents ... They, um ...

items.speaker: Government Employee
items.text: Anyway, just follow us. We'll take you to them. Quickly.
Drawers open and close in rapid succession as the presence seems to follow their orders. After the last one is closed, the two men escort the invisible child outside.
The clock stops ticking.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I think that might be all that's left of his memories.
Maxim at last turns to face them, though he gives them only a single empty glance before he staggers back toward the grandfather clock. This time, however, one of them stands in his way.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Who are you people?! Leave me alone!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Maxim, you can still save lives before it's too late. It's time to let go.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Why?

items.speaker: Tableware
items.text: Why?
Maxim's voice booms out everywhere and all at once. Even the knives and forks on the table clatter with his voice.

items.speaker: Tableware
items.text: The day I left with those men, I saw my neighbor hugging her mother. She was back from the hospital. I remember they had a robot carrying their suitcases, one just like my father made.

items.speaker: Tableware
items.text: She survived. She didn't leave her child alone.

items.speaker: Tableware
items.text: Why me?

items.speaker: Tableware
items.text: Why my family?! It isn't right!

items.speaker: Tableware
items.text: My mother had saved her!

items.speaker: Little Robot
items.text: My father made the robots that took care of them.

items.speaker: Tableware & Little Robot
items.text: But they didn't get to come home.

items.speaker: Little Robot
items.text: They left me alone. All I had to remember them were the tattered medals the government gave me on their behalf.

items.speaker: Tableware
items.text: I never learned where they were buried. They could be lying in some unknown, unmarked pit or burned away to ash!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I know all too well how painful it can be to accept your loved ones' sacrifice. But we have a responsibility to ensure their deaths were not in vain.
The tableware and the little robot collapse suddenly.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: A few memorials, a few medals, then things changed. People stopped remembering. They started saying that it was the Kollektiv that saved them.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: That's right! The Kollektiv. Hahaha .... The Kollektiv.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: What a glorious, heartwarming name! It brings to mind all of those soldiers marching in lockstep in the celebratory parades.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Thud, thud, thud! "Behold our march to the future, comrades! We will build a new world forged by our hands! Aren't we all so proud of the 'collective'!"

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: People's heads became filled with these lies. They forgot all that we had gone through, or maybe they just wanted to forget. Then the monuments changed. Suddenly they all had his face—his name.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: There was no room for any others. Names became mere statistics. Mothers and fathers, children; dead and forgotten in their millions. But not him. He was "Dr. Sechenov, inventor of polymer, savior of the Soviet Union."

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Over and over, all the glory, all the praise, everything went to him and his damned polymer.
Maxim twists, kicking the dining table with enough force to rattle the dishes.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: How can that be? Why does he live when they had to die? How can we go blindly into this world he created?

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Their graves were just stepping stones on his march of progress.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Men like Sechenov only look forward to their "bright and limitless future." To them, the sooner the dead are forgotten, the better.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That isn't true, Maxim.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Of course, the ones that survive should mourn and honor those they lost. But we also have to move on. Not to forget, but to build again.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You let yourself be trapped in the shadow of your loss, but I know your parents wouldn't have wanted that for you.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: Don't tell me what they'd think!
Black smoke billows out from Maxim's body as it begins to fall apart before their eyes. The inky smoke coalesces and takes on human forms.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: It's easy for people like you to say that—to pretend that a few kind words are enough to bury the dead.

items.speaker: Maxim
items.text: But then you praise the man that took everything from them. It isn't fair!
